transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came in because… honestly, I got really scared. At first I thought maybe I was just tired or maybe the house was making noises, you know, like pipes or the hallway settling, but I’ve been hearing my name being called from the hallway at home when nobody is there. And it’s not like a thought in my head or like I’m imagining it on purpose—it sounds real. Like, as real as if my husband was standing right next to me saying my name.

And then it happened once at the warehouse too, where I work, and that really shook me because I looked around and there wasn’t anyone there who could’ve said it. I keep trying to explain it away, but it felt so clear, and it scared me enough that I thought I should come talk to someone before it gets worse or before I start feeling like I can’t trust what I’m hearing.
Have you started believing that someone is trying to harm you or watch you?

I don’t… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been nervous because the voice thing scared me, so I do catch myself paying more attention to noises or looking around more than I normally would. But I wouldn’t say I believe someone is trying to hurt me or that somebody’s watching me, not exactly.

It’s more like I feel unsettled and I’m trying to figure out what’s happening, if that makes sense. Like I’ll hear something and then I’ll check, but I’m not thinking there’s a person out to get me. At least I don’t think I am.
Did these voices start after you used any drugs or alcohol?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think so, but I guess I don’t know exactly what counts. Like, I wasn’t sitting there thinking, “Oh, I used something and now I’m hearing this,” if that’s what you mean.

I’ve been trying to think back and connect it to something—being tired, stress, noises in the building, that kind of thing—but I haven’t really noticed a clear connection with drugs or alcohol. It didn’t feel like that to me. It just kind of started happening, and that’s part of why it scared me, because I couldn’t explain it.
Do you ever hear your name being called only when you’re just falling asleep or just waking up?

No, I don’t think it’s only then. I mean, I’ve heard of that, like when you’re half-asleep and your mind does weird things, and I honestly wish that was all it was. But what scared me is it’s happened when I was up and moving around, like at home hearing my name called from the hallway when nobody was there.

And once it happened at the warehouse too, while I was at work, not falling asleep or waking up or anything. It sounded real—like somebody was actually right there saying my name, like my husband would if he was standing beside me. That’s why I couldn’t just brush it off as a sleep thing.
Have you had a recent illness, fever, head injury, or seizure?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, not that I know of. I haven’t had anything where I was like, “Oh, I’m really sick,” or running a fever or anything like that recently. No head injury that I can think of either—like I didn’t fall and hit my head, or get into an accident or anything.

And seizures… I don’t think I’ve ever had one, at least not that anyone has told me. I guess I don’t totally know what all counts as a seizure, but I haven’t had anything obvious like blacking out or shaking or waking up confused somewhere. So, no, nothing like that that I’m aware of.
Have you started believing things that other people say aren’t true?

Yeah… I guess so, if I’m being honest. Not like I thought the sky was purple or anything like that, but I got really convinced about this plan I had with my crafts.

I do little craft things, and I started thinking, like, no, this isn’t just a hobby, this is the thing. I was sure I could turn it into a real retirement business right away, like basically solve this whole future-money problem for our family. In my head it felt so obvious, like I had figured out the perfect plan and everyone else was just going to see it once I explained it right.

And other people were more cautious, like, “Maybe slow down,” or “That’s not realistic yet,” and I remember feeling kind of offended, honestly. Like they just didn’t understand that I had already worked it all out. Looking back, I can see maybe I was jumping way ahead, but at the time it felt completely true to me.
Around the time this started, did you feel unusually energetic or “up” for days at a time?

Yeah… I did. At least at first, that’s kind of exactly how it felt. I was really fired up, like I had this engine in me, and everything seemed clear and possible all at once. Especially with the craft business idea—I wasn’t just excited like, “Oh, this could be fun.” It was more like, “No, this is it, I can do this, I can make this work, and I need to get moving on it now.”

And it wasn’t only the crafts. I got really intense about things at home too, like house rules and how things should be done. I felt like I was finally seeing what needed to happen, and if everyone would just get on board, things would be better.

But I wasn’t exactly cheerful the whole time. I was “up,” but also really easily irritated. My husband could make some tiny comment—something that probably wasn’t even meant badly—and I would snap at him like he was trying to shut me down or hold me back. In the moment it felt like he was standing in the way, even if he was just asking a normal question. So yes, I felt unusually energetic and driven, but it also came with this edge, like I was ready to argue if anyone slowed me down.
Before this high-energy period started, have you ever had a time lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… yes, I think so. It’s not like it was just a bad day here or there. The depressed, kind of withdrawn part has been hanging over me for about three months, I’d say.

It’s hard to explain because it wasn’t always the exact same every single day, but most days I felt like I was under this cloud, like I just wanted to pull back from everything. And then these past few weeks made it much harder to manage, like the whole thing got sharper or heavier or something.

So if you’re asking if it was more than two weeks, then yes. Definitely more than two weeks. More like months.
Did the voice started only during the time when you felt unusually energetic and driven?

Yes… the voice thing was during that really wound-up stretch. Like when I was barely sleeping and I felt like I had to keep going, keep talking, keep fixing everything, like I couldn’t slow down even if people wanted me to.

That was when I heard my name being called. It wasn’t happening before all that started, not that I remember. And then later, when I kind of crashed into being more low and withdrawn, I wasn’t hearing voices then either. I also didn’t have that same kind of certainty about those big ideas during the low period.

So, yes, as far as I can tell, the voice calling my name was tied to that energetic, driven time.
